intended_object: The docstring and the module doc describe the embedding of the coefficient field C = k(unweighted variables, ratios x_j/x_i for j ∈ S \ {i}) into the valuation ring of the weight-one valuation on K = Frac(k[σ]). It is the map a ↦ (constant rational function a, pulled back to K through the birational coordinates). It is a coefficient-field section of the residue map.
explanation:
The body composes `RatFunc.C : C →+* RatFunc C` with the inverse of the coordinate isomorphism `weightOneCoordinates : K ≃+* RatFunc C`. It then restricts the codomain to the valuation subring of `weightOneValuation`. The proof that this restriction is allowed is the right one: by definition (`weightOneValuation_apply`), `weightOneValuation` is the X-adic valuation on `RatFunc C` transported along the coordinate isomorphism. Constants are polynomials, so the X-adic valuation is ≤ 1 on them.

So the result is exactly the ring hom the docstring describes: constants of the coefficient field, viewed in K, lie in the valuation ring. The library later uses it to show that the residue field is isomorphic to C (`weightOneResidueEquiv`). For that, the section composed with the residue map is the identity.

The map is specific to this particular valuation and coordinate system, and its content needs that setting. Mathlib has no general counterpart for this concrete embedding. It is close to an auxiliary device, but it is a genuine mathematical map, and it is defined correctly.
